product_context: CitySocial is a modular-monolith social platform for city residents (currently Austin), built as one Rails app whose features live as near-independent modules (mountable engines) under components/. platform_core owns identity (User), the Follow social graph, a public Graph API, and an event bus; feed is the reference module (posts + timeline); communities is subreddit-style (join, post, comment, up/down vote); marketplace is classified listings with photos; restaurants is head-to-head Elo ranking of local spots. Users are residents who follow each other and engage through these modules. 'Better' means tightening the existing engagement loops (do -> others see it -> they get notified/react), filling in missing empty/loading/error and accessibility states on views that already ship, and polishing the UX of already-shipped modules. It does NOT mean speculative net-new features nobody asked for. Every view must compose the PlatformCore::Ui components and Tailwind v4 design tokens (no hand-rolled markup, no hardcoded hex). Modules may depend only on platform_core and must cross boundaries only via events or a sibling's app/public API (Packwerk enforces this).
out_of_scope: Anything touching auth, authorization, sessions, or payments
Standing up a whole new module (that is the human-run /new-app-module flow)
Cross-module references that violate the Packwerk boundary contract
Editing the @theme design tokens or the standalone Tailwind build config

items.title: Give icon-only vote buttons accessible labels
items.problem: The upvote/downvote controls are icon-only glyphs with no accessible name.
items.evidence: components/communities/app/views/communities/posts/_vote.html.erb:4,8 — up/down glyphs rendered with no aria-label
acceptance: ButtonComponent accepts an optional aria_label:
The vote buttons expose aria-label Upvote/Downvote

items.title: Add empty state to the restaurants leaderboard
items.problem: The restaurants leaderboard rendered a bare, header-only table when there were no restaurants.
items.evidence: components/restaurants/app/views/restaurants/leaderboard/index.html.erb:9 — TableComponent iterated @restaurants with no any? guard and no EmptyState
acceptance: With no restaurants, /restaurants/leaderboard renders an EmptyState
When restaurants exist, the ranked table renders as before

items.title: Add select support to FormFieldComponent
items.problem: Dropdowns were hand-rolled label+select markup, bypassing the design system and showing no inline validation errors.
items.evidence: form_field_component.rb:6 INPUT_TYPES excludes select; marketplace/listings/_form.html.erb:13-19 and communities/communities/new.html.erb:8-9 hand-roll f.select; Marketplace::Listing validates category presence (listing.rb:19) yet the select showed no inline error
acceptance: FormFieldComponent accepts type: :select with a collection and renders a styled select
A select with a validation error shows the inline error + border-danger
type: :select without a collection raises ArgumentError
Marketplace listing form and new-community form use FormFieldComponent for their selects
/design documents the select option

items.title: Vote control reflects the current user's own vote
items.problem: The up/down vote buttons look identical whether or not the current user has already voted, so casting a vote gives no visual confirmation — breaking the do -> see-it-reflected loop.
items.evidence: components/communities/app/models/communities/votable.rb:24 — vote_value_for(user_id) already returns -1/0/1, but components/communities/app/views/communities/posts/_vote.html.erb renders both arrows the same regardless. No schema change needed.
acceptance: When the current user has upvoted, the up arrow renders in an active (highlighted) state; likewise the down arrow when downvoted
Anonymous users and un-voted items render the neutral state as today
Applies on the community post list, the post show page, and comments
Covered by a request/component spec asserting the active state renders for the voter

items.title: External ticket/detail links open in a new tab
items.problem: The events 'Tickets & details' CTA (and other external links) navigate away from CitySocial in the same tab, losing the user's place — an engagement leak. Community post URLs already open in a new tab with rel=noopener; events don't.
items.evidence: components/events/app/views/events/events/show.html.erb:32 — external @event.url button has no target/rel, vs communities/app/views/communities/posts/show.html.erb:17 which uses target=_blank rel=noopener
acceptance: External event ticket links open in a new tab with rel=noopener noreferrer
Internal links are unchanged
Covered by a request spec asserting target/rel on the ticket link
items.notes: F-001 (PR #2) has merged, so the ButtonComponent-conflict hold is lifted. Still needs ButtonComponent to accept target:/rel: (it currently only takes variant/size/href/method/params/confirm/type/aria_label/pressed) — add that passthrough as part of the item.

items.title: Semantic <time> timestamps with exact-date tooltips
items.problem: Relative timestamps (time_ago_in_words) render as plain text with no machine-readable datetime and no hover-to-see-exact-date.
items.evidence: feed/posts/index.html.erb:10, communities/communities/show.html.erb:38, communities/posts/show.html.erb:14,52, marketplace/listings/show.html.erb:45 — 'X ago' rendered as bare text, no <time datetime title>
acceptance: Relative timestamps wrap a <time datetime=...> element with a title showing the exact date/time
Rendered text is unchanged
Covered by a spec on at least one surface

items.title: Create public resident profiles with avatars
items.problem: Residents have no public identity surface beyond a handle, so their activity across CitySocial lacks context, trust, and a consistent way to discover who is participating.
items.evidence: Explicit human priority in the CitySocial Codex product-loop mission: public user profile with avatar; profile fields must stay optional and never expose email or hidden PII.
acceptance: A resident can edit only their own optional display name, neighborhood, bio, and avatar
Avatar uploads accept JPEG, PNG, or WebP up to 5 MB and invalid files render inline errors
Anyone can view /people/:handle with public fields and follow counts, but never email or authentication data
The shared AvatarComponent and author links make profiles discoverable from the navigation, feed, communities, and marketplace
A PII-safe PlatformCore::Graph.public_profile API and platform_core.profile_updated event expose the capability across module boundaries
Model, request, public API, and component specs cover the complete flow
items.notes: Persona: city resident participating across multiple modules. Job: understand who another resident is and present a consistent public identity. Loop: resident updates profile -> activity links bring others to it -> public identity context supports follows and reactions; profile updates publish for future notification/search subscribers.

items.title: Create a follower activity notifications inbox
items.problem: Residents have no durable way to learn when people they follow publish activity across CitySocial, so the social loop ends at creation instead of bringing others back to react.
items.evidence: docs/roadmap.md Next explicitly promises a notifications module subscribing to feed.post_created and communities.post_created and fanning out to followers; both events and PlatformCore::Graph.follower_ids already exist.
acceptance: A generated Notifications engine owns an additive, reversible notification schema and depends only on platform_core
Feed and community post events asynchronously create one idempotent notification for each follower, never the actor or non-followers
Signed-in residents have an inbox with unread count, empty state, recent activity, per-item read-through, and mark-all-read actions built from shared UI components
Residents can read only their own notifications, and stored destinations are restricted to internal paths
Model, delivery, event wiring, public API, and request specs cover the complete flow
items.notes: Persona: a city resident following neighbors across modules. Job: notice relevant activity and return to it without monitoring every product. Loop: followed resident posts -> Notifications consumes the event and fans out -> follower opens the inbox and returns to react. Expansion path: marketplace activity, feedback updates, mentions, delivery preferences, and grouping.

items.title: Add Top sorting to community comments
items.problem: Community conversations can only show comments chronologically even though comment vote scores are already stored, so the most useful responses stay buried.
items.evidence: research.md#R-001; components/communities/app/models/communities/comment.rb defines only chronological while its Votable concern maintains score.
acceptance: Communities::Comment gets a top scope ordering by score descending and created_at descending
The post page offers New and Top query-param sorting while keeping New as the default
Changing sort order does not alter vote casting
Model and request specs cover both orders

items.title: Filter the restaurant leaderboard by cuisine
items.problem: Residents cannot narrow restaurant rankings to comparable cuisines even though every restaurant already stores cuisine.
items.evidence: research.md#R-002; components/restaurants/app/controllers/restaurants/leaderboard_controller.rb accepts no filter while restaurants_restaurants.cuisine is already populated and displayed.
acceptance: The leaderboard accepts a cuisine query param through a by_cuisine scope
A shared FormFieldComponent select lists cuisines present in the catalog
No selection preserves the complete leaderboard
A request spec proves the selected cuisine narrows results

items.title: Add event calendar actions
items.problem: Residents who discover an event cannot carry it into their calendar, making it easy to forget after leaving CitySocial.
items.evidence: research.md#R-003; components/events/app/views/events/events/show.html.erb has ticket details but no calendar action despite complete start, optional end, venue, and description fields.
acceptance: Event detail adds a Google Calendar link built from existing event fields
A read-only controller action downloads a valid ICS file with a defined fallback end time
Existing ticket behavior remains unchanged
Request specs cover both calendar formats and the fallback

items.title: Let sellers renew stale marketplace listings
items.problem: Marketplace sellers must recreate a stale listing to restore visibility even though the existing timestamps and expiration already support a safe renewal flow.
items.evidence: research.md#R-004; components/marketplace/app/models/marketplace/listing.rb already owns expiration and recent ordering, and mark_sold provides the owner-action pattern.
acceptance: An owner-only renew action resurfaces the listing and extends expiration by 30 days
Renewal is blocked for sold listings and within 48 hours of creation or renewal
The existing owner actions show Renew only when eligible
Model and request specs cover timestamps, ownership, sold state, and cooldown
items.notes: Consumed R-004 (grader 10/10). renew! resets created_at (doubles as the 48h cooldown clock, no migration) and pushes expires_at 30 days out; owner-only via the existing require_owner guard; Renew button rendered only when renewable?. Reused codex-assigned id F-012 to stay consistent with open PR #12, which had queued F-009-F-012 (ready) but implemented none of them.

items.title: Create private resident messaging
items.problem: Residents can discover and react to one another across CitySocial, but they have no private place to coordinate a meetup, marketplace handoff, or neighbor-to-neighbor follow-up.
items.evidence: docs/roadmap.md Next explicitly promises a messaging module for resident-to-resident conversations, and public resident profiles now provide the safe identity surface and entry point.
acceptance: A generated Messaging engine owns an additive, reversible one-to-one conversation and message schema and depends only on platform_core
A signed-in resident can start a conversation from another resident's public profile or handle and send an initial message
Participants can view one shared thread, reply, and see unread state in an owner-scoped inbox while non-participants cannot read or write it
Unknown and self recipients plus blank or oversized messages render inline errors without creating records
messaging.message_created publishes participant and record IDs but never private message content
Model, public API, request, route, event, and module-boundary checks cover the complete flow
items.notes: Persona: a city resident who needs to coordinate privately after discovering a neighbor, seller, or community member. Job: move a public connection into a safe one-to-one follow-up without sharing email or hidden PII. Loop: resident sends -> recipient sees unread state/event -> recipient opens and replies. Messaging deserves a separate product surface because private conversation history, read state, access control, and future safety controls are distinct from public feed/community content.

items.title: Batch-load the viewer's votes on the community post list
items.problem: Rendering the community post list now calls vote_value_for(current_user.id) once per post (and per comment), issuing one communities_votes lookup per row — an N+1 that grows with the page size.
items.evidence: components/communities/app/views/communities/communities/show.html.erb:30 and posts/show.html.erb:11,56 — each `<record>.vote_value_for(current_user&.id)` runs a separate indexed SELECT inside the @posts / @comments loop (introduced with F-004).
acceptance: The viewer's votes for a page of posts/comments are loaded in a single query and passed into the vote partial
Rendered vote highlighting is unchanged from F-004
Covered by a spec asserting the vote query count does not grow with the number of rows
items.notes: Below the 1.0 schedule threshold; grounded and honest but low-value (one indexed lookup per row). Strengthen or split if it ever matters; do not force-schedule.

items.title: Add messaging inbox management
items.problem: As conversation history grows, residents will need a way to find active threads and clear inactive ones from the primary inbox.
items.evidence: F-013 messaging milestone 1 intentionally caps the inbox at 50 recent conversations and ships no archive or search controls.
acceptance: A participant can archive and restore a conversation only for their own inbox
Inbox search matches the other participant's public handle or display name without exposing private identity fields
Archived conversations remain readable by direct participant access and return to the inbox when a new reply arrives

items.title: Carry public context into new conversations
items.problem: A message started from a listing or community post can lose the public context that prompted the resident to reach out.
items.evidence: F-013 establishes a profile/handle conversation entry point but intentionally stores no sibling record references or context links.
acceptance: Messaging accepts a validated internal context path and short public context label when a conversation starts
The thread header links back to that context without reading a sibling model
Marketplace and communities can pass context through URL parameters without adding module dependencies

items.title: Feedback 'Support' toggle emits aria-pressed
items.problem: The feedback 'Support' button is a toggle whose supported/unsupported state is conveyed only by color and label swap, so assistive-tech users get no pressed-state signal.
items.evidence: components/feedback/app/views/feedback/submissions/_submission.html.erb:4-9 and components/feedback/app/views/feedback/submissions/show.html.erb:41 — the support ButtonComponent switches variant (:primary/:secondary) on `supported` but never sets pressed:. ButtonComponent now accepts pressed: (F-004, PR #13), so this is a one-line wire-up per call.
acceptance: The support button on the feedback list and show page renders aria-pressed=true when the current user supports it, false otherwise
The existing variant swap and supports_count display are unchanged
Covered by a request spec asserting aria-pressed reflects support state
items.notes: Depends on ButtonComponent#pressed: shipping via F-004 (PR #13). PR #13 has now merged, so the hold is lifted and this is schedulable. Renumbered from F-013 while resolving PR #15 so the shipped Messaging feature keeps the ID used by its PR and progress record. Reconciled to done in the F-011 run: open draft PR #19 already implements it.
